Surname Position in a Two-Token Name

Source: R/parse_one_name.R
two_token_surname.Rd

Keeps the written order (first name, then surname) unless the census makes it much more likely that the name is written surname first.

Usage

two_token_surname(x, data)

Arguments

x

A length-2 character vector of name tokens.

data

Census rows for x, as returned by get_census_data().

Value

The position (1 or 2) of the surname.

Details

Each token gets a smoothed surname share, s = (last + a) / (first + last + 2a), with pseudo-count a = .order_pseudo_count, so thin evidence moves toward 0.5 (RUVIN, with 106 first-name records, no longer reads as a given name). A token absent from the census gets s = .order_unlisted_share. The tokens are swapped only when the odds that the name is written surname first, s1 (1 - s2) / ((1 - s1) s2), exceed .order_prior_odds; two-word Form 990 Part VII names are written first name first about 98% of the time. An unlisted first token of one or two letters is initials (HM CHERRY, J MARKEL), and a lone letter elsewhere gets s = .order_initial_share (BISHOP J -> surname BISHOP; THOMAS H keeps H, a middle initial left after a stripped surname).

The settings were tuned on 758,388 two-word Part VII names labelled by the convention of the other names on the same return: see data-raw/name_order_eval.R and NEWS.md.
